name: Prestige Beauty Product Launch Campaign
description: A soft-luxury beauty launch system combining category insight, product and ingredient storytelling, audience art direction, creator distribution, and a measured go-to-market cadence.
style_guide:
# Prestige Beauty Product Launch Campaign

## Design intent

Create a refined go-to-market deck for prestige skincare, cosmetics, fragrance, or personal-care launches. The visual language is quiet soft luxury: warm ivory paper, champagne and rose-beige surfaces, espresso typography, luminous product still life, editorial italics, generous spacing, and small pieces of clinical or commercial evidence. The story should move from consumer opportunity to product truth, audience and visual world, creator and channel plan, then launch cadence, budget, and measurable outcomes.

The reference previews are visual-language examples only. Do not reuse their brand, product, formula, ingredients, clinical results, model, persona, quotations, channels, creator counts, budget, sales targets, dates, or KPIs. All claims and launch content must come from the current workspace and the applicable evidence and approvals.

## Canvas and grid

- Use a fixed `1280 × 720 px` 16:9 canvas with `62–72 px` side margins, `34–42 px` top brand framing, and `24–30 px` for sources and legal notes.
- Use a 12-column grid with `18–24 px` gutters. Align product imagery, ingredient modules, evidence cards, portrait crops, creator tiers, channel splits, timelines, budgets, and KPI cards.
- Reserve `110–145 px` for the section label, editorial headline, and one concise supporting line. Allow one strong visual or exhibit to dominate the lower field.
- Prefer balanced `6/6` cover compositions, `7/5` chart-and-insight pages, three-part product stories, portrait-plus-profile pages, and full-width launch timelines.
- Use `24–32 px` between major modules and `12–18 px` within cards. Negative space is part of the premium system and should not be filled with decoration.
- Body pages should remain light. Use one espresso panel only for a decisive commercial or narrative conclusion.

## Color system

### Core palette

- Warm beauty ivory: `#F7F2EA`. Use for the primary canvas and spacious editorial ground.
- Porcelain white: `#FFFDFC`. Use for clinical evidence, charts, KPI cards, and clean product surfaces.
- Champagne beige: `#C6A07D`. Use for key phrases, timeline nodes, creator tiers, and refined commercial emphasis.
- Blush rose: `#E8C6C0`. Use for secondary surfaces, audience mood, beauty imagery, and one soft chart series.
- Rose gold: `#B78366`. Use sparingly for product detail, selected values, and launch highlights.
- Espresso brown: `#3A2F2B`. Use for primary typography, decisive panels, and high-contrast labels.
- Warm taupe: `#8F8178`. Use for secondary text, legends, and source context.

### Semantic use

- Champagne and rose gold signal priority or premium craft; they do not prove efficacy or performance.
- Blush is an atmospheric surface, not a gender code or a blanket audience assumption.
- Use green only for a verified favorable result and red only for a validated safety or performance concern.
- Maintain sufficient contrast. Long copy should be espresso on ivory or white, never low-contrast beige on blush.

## Typography

- Use `Aptos`, `Inter`, `Helvetica Neue`, or another elegant neutral sans-serif.
- Use a restrained italic cut of the same family for one phrase in major headlines, product names, editorial conclusions, or campaign themes. Avoid decorative scripts.
- Cover title: `50–62 px`, regular. Page headline: `32–40 px`, regular to medium. Brand or section label: `9–11 px`, uppercase, tracked. Body: `14–17 px`. Evidence and tables: `10–13 px`. Legal and sources: `8–10 px`.
- Keep paragraphs short and airy. Use medium weight for product truth and evidence, not for every label.
- Numeric outcomes should use tabular figures with measurement, period, comparator, and status kept nearby.

## Components

- Cards are flat white or pale-blush rectangles with thin warm-gray rules, minimal corner radius, and no shadow.
- Product modules combine a controlled pack shot, a concise proposition, ingredient or feature logic, and a separate evidence field.
- Ingredient rows should include name, concentration only when approved, role, source or test basis, and any required qualifier.
- Consumer insight cards use a numbered finding, one piece of evidence, and a launch implication.
- Creator tables should show tier, role, deliverable, audience fit, usage rights, count, and budget basis.
- KPI cards must state metric definition, target or actual status, time window, and data source.

## Charts and diagrams

- Favor restrained category bars, consumer insight lists, ingredient-benefit chains, clinical-result panels, persona or audience profiles, moodboard grids, creator-tier tables, channel mix bars, launch timelines, budget donuts, and KPI scorecards.
- Charts should use champagne, blush, taupe, and espresso with direct labels and quiet gridlines.
- Clinical or consumer-test exhibits must show study type, sample, duration, comparator, endpoint, units, statistical status when relevant, and responsible qualifier.
- Channel and creator views should distinguish paid, owned, earned, affiliate, seeding, sampling, and retail support.
- Launch timelines need gates for formula, packaging, claims, production, inventory, retailer or platform readiness, content, media, and measurement.
- Avoid 3D charts, crowded radar charts, vanity-metric gauges, and decorative scientific diagrams.

## Composition families

### Soft-luxury cover

Split the page between an ivory title field and a luminous still life of the actual product or a rights-cleared conceptual substitute. Use one italic champagne phrase and keep presenter, company, date, and confidentiality restrained.

### Market and consumer lens

Pair a simple category trend chart with three numbered consumer or market shifts. State the launch implication in the headline and separate sourced evidence from strategic interpretation.

### Product truth

Use a hero pack shot, three or fewer ingredient or feature modules, and one evidence panel. Keep the proposition understandable before presenting technical detail.

### Audience and visual direction

Pair one representative audience portrait or behavior-led profile with a concise persona, a still-life moodboard, and a small campaign palette. Avoid inventing a named fictional consumer as if research had validated them.

### Creator and channel strategy

Use a row of content-pillar crops beside a creator-tier table and a proportional channel split. Connect each tier and channel to a job in the funnel and defined deliverables.

### Launch cadence, budget, and KPIs

Use a four-phase horizontal timeline above a budget allocation and outcome cards. End with a concise ambition or decision statement, not an unsupported superlative.

## Imagery

- Favor rights-cleared pack shots, texture macros, ingredient still lifes, skin or application detail, quiet portraiture, and tactile materials such as silk, stone, glass, petals, water, or brushed metal when relevant to the product.
- Keep lighting soft, directional, and warm with controlled highlights. Preserve real skin texture and accurate product color.
- Crop portraits cleanly and use them to communicate behavior or campaign direction, not to imply unverified endorsement.
- Use one minimal line-icon family only where a photograph or label would be less clear.
- Avoid over-retouched skin, impossible product scale, generic spa imagery, laboratory clichés, medical imagery, excessive flowers, and unrelated luxury accessories.

## Content integrity

- Do not invent formula, ingredients, concentration, sourcing, safety, tolerability, efficacy, clinical results, consumer preference, dermatologist support, awards, regulatory status, sustainability, sales, creator reach, budget, or KPI outcomes.
- Distinguish in vitro, instrumental, clinical, dermatologist-supervised, consumer-perception, and marketing claims. State sample, duration, comparator, endpoint, units, and limitations.
- Do not turn correlation, ingredient literature, or a supplier claim into finished-product efficacy.
- Use only approved product names, INCI or ingredient terminology, claims, imagery, disclaimers, and market-specific language.
- Audience and persona claims must cite research scope, market, sample, and date. Creator reach must distinguish followers, views, unique reach, engagement, and attributable sales.
- Financial and channel pages must clarify currency, gross or net sales, returns, retailer margin, media fees, production, sampling, rights, agency cost, and contingency.
- If evidence is missing, omit the claim or label it `concept`, `hypothesis`, `target`, `illustrative`, `planned`, or `pending substantiation`. Never invent data to fill a proof card.

## Avoid

- Do not copy preview brands, products, ingredients, claims, percentages, personas, faces, quotes, creator tiers, budgets, dates, channels, or KPIs.
- Do not present cosmetic benefits as medical treatment or use before-and-after implications without compliant substantiation.
- Do not use blush as the only audience signal or assume beauty consumers share one gender, age, skin type, or purchase motivation.
- Do not use low-contrast beige type, excessive italics, ornamental scripts, glossy gradients, glass cards, heavy shadows, or oversized rounded corners.
- Do not overcrowd a premium page with more product claims, creator logos, or ingredient badges than the evidence supports.
- Do not let still-life imagery substitute for product differentiation, commercial logic, launch readiness, or measurement.
- Do not hide required legal qualifiers in unreadable footnotes.
